To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the use of a combination of analytical and bioinformatic approaches is essential for the identification of secondary metabolites, (b) the use of these approaches in the study of the tomato fruit has revealed a large and complex array of secondary metabolites that are not well characterized in this fruit, (c) the identification of the genes encoding the enzymes responsible for their synthesis and the enzymes involved in their catabolism will enable the elucidation of the pathways involved in their biosynthesis and
the metabolome of the tomato fruit is highly complex and that the metabolic shifts that occur during development of the tomato fruit are not restricted to primary metabolism.

the tomato genome sequence has been used in combination with a range of metabolomics strategies in order to better understand the regulation and function(s) of secondary metabolism during tomato fruit development and ripeness.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the genes and enzymes responsible for the synthesis and degradation of secondary metabolites during tomato fruit development and ripenings and with the elucidation of the role of these metabolites during this process.
the identification, characterization and manipulation of secondary metabolic pathways in the tomato.
the regulation of the tomato secondary metabolome and its role in the development of fruit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metabolic changes which occur during tomato fruit development have not been fully characterized.
the role of secondary metabolites during fruit development is not yet known.
the metabolic shifts underpining tomato fruit development and ripeness are still not well understood, but that the tools are now available to make great strides in this area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the tomato genome sequence has enabled us to develop metabolomics strategies that have provided new information on tomato secondary metabolism and that this information is being exploited to better understand the role of these metabolites during tomato fruit development.

we have been able to use the genome sequence to identify genes involved in secondary metabolism and then use metabolomics to confirm that these genes do indeed encode for the enzymes that are responsible for the production of the compounds of interest.
we are still in the process of identifying and quantifying the secondary metabolites present in the fruit.
The main takeaway from our work is that

metabolomic strategies can be successfully employed to identify and quantify secondary metabolites in tomato fruits and that these strategies are likely to be particularly useful in elucidating the role of these metabolites during development.
the tomato genome sequence provides a powerful tool for metabolite identification.
the tomato genome sequence has enabled the development of metabolomics strategies which will facilitate our understanding of the role of secondary metabolism in tomato fruit development.
